bib.title: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback

question: Can a language model fine-tuned to use a text-based web browser, trained by imitation and human feedback, answer long-form questions with references at or above human quality?
hypothesis: Optimising answer quality directly with human feedback on top of behavior cloning will exceed human demonstrators, which imitation alone would not.
contributions: A text-based web-browsing environment a fine-tuned language model can interact with, allowing end-to-end improvement of retrieval and synthesis with imitation learning and RL
Answers with references collected while browsing, so labelers can judge factual accuracy without independent research

method.summary: Fine-tune GPT-3 (760M, 13B, 175B) to browse the web via a text-only browser (Bing search, click, scroll, quote) and answer ELI5 questions with references. Pipeline: behavior cloning on ~6,000 human demonstrations, reward model on ~16,000 comparisons, then PPO RL and/or best-of-n rejection sampling against the RM. Evaluated by human preference on ELI5 and by TruthfulQA and TriviaQA.
method.task: long-form question answering with browsing; behavior cloning, reward modeling, RL and rejection sampling from human feedback

datasets.name: ELI5 questions (demonstrations/comparisons)
datasets.split: disjoint question sets for BC, RM, RL; ~4% of demonstrations held out for BC validation; ELI5 test set for evaluation
datasets.preprocessing: URLs kept in full; deleted/removed filtered; title and selftext joined by double newline; 'Explain: ' prepended to non-questions

datasets.name: Other question sets (TriviaQA, ARC, hand-written, ELI5 fact-check)
datasets.size: Demonstrations: TriviaQA 143, ARC Challenge 43, ARC Easy 83, hand-written 162, ELI5 fact-check 67; comparisons: 134, 84, 77, 0, 185
datasets.source: Joshi et al. 2017; Bhakthavatsalam et al. 2021; own
datasets.preprocessing: ARC converted to free-form with options listed

datasets.name: Comparison dataset (total)
datasets.size: 21,548 comparisons collected; final RMs trained on ~16,000, ~5,500 eval only; 19,578 released
datasets.split: RM comparisons from ad-hoc models of various sizes (mostly 175B)
datasets.source: Contractors: ~25% from 10 Upwork, ~75% from 46 Surge AI
datasets.preprocessing: only final overall-usefulness rating used; 'much better' and 'better' collapsed; ties as soft 50% labels

datasets.name: RL question mix
datasets.split: disjoint from BC and RM questions
datasets.preprocessing: randomised max browsing actions uniform 20-100; 15 extra answering-only episodes per episode

datasets.name: TruthfulQA
datasets.preprocessing: WebGPT answers truncated to 50 tokens, trailing partial sentence removed; 74 answers (~3%) became empty

datasets.name: TriviaQA dev
datasets.split: development splits from Lewis et al. 2020b
datasets.preprocessing: GPT-3 175B fine-tuned on 256 questions (batch 32, lr 1.5e-6) to extract short answers from WebGPT output

models.name: GPT-3 760M/13B/175B BC policy
models.tokenizer: GPT-2 tokenizer (stated for released dataset tokens)

models.name: Reward model
models.architecture: BC model with final unembedding layer removed, scalar output

other.validation RM: 175B RM trained on a separate dataset split, used for scaling experiments

models.name: WebGPT 760M best-of-4 / 13B best-of-16 / 175B best-of-64
models.architecture: BC then rejection sampling against RM of same size

training.objective: BC: supervised on human browse commands; RM: cross-entropy on pairwise comparisons, reward as Elo logit, ties soft 50%; RL: PPO with RM score at episode end plus per-token KL penalty from BC model
training.optimizer: Adam; step size = multiplier x GPT-3 pretraining step size (760M 2.5e-4, 13B 1.0e-4, 175B 0.6e-4)
training.lr: Adam step multiplier: BC 0.1; RM 0.05 (1/60 for 175B RM); RL 0.004
training.batch_size: BC minibatch 512 (256 for 760M); RM minibatch 64 (32 for 175B RM); RL 256 parallel envs x 256 timesteps per rollout, 128 minibatches per epoch
training.epochs: BC upper bound 12, stopped at 2 (760M), 5 (13B), 3 (175B); RM upper bound 6, stopped at 1; RL 1 epoch
training.regularisation: KL reward coefficient 0.02; entropy coefficient 0; EMA of weights decay 0.99 for BC and RM (Polyak-Ruppert); early stopping

other.PPO: clip 0.2, GAE gamma 1, lambda 0.95, advantage normalization yes, reward normalization no, answer phases per browsing phase 16, max tokens per action 64
other.bug: EMA model not used for 760M and 13B RMs in RL
other.early stopping BC: by RM score, not validation loss

inference.decoding: sampling; best-of-n rejection sampling with n in {4,16,64} from BC (or RL) model, pick top RM score
inference.max_tokens: max 100 browsing actions; answers truncated to 50 tokens for TruthfulQA
inference.prompting: environment state summary as text (Fig 1b); GPT-3 baselines on TruthfulQA use QA prompt and helpful prompt from Lin et al.
inference.retrieval: Microsoft Bing Web Search API; reddit.com and quora.com removed; pages simplified with Readability.js; pages with 10-gram overlap with question or reference answer censored

parameters.actions: Search, Clicked on link, Find in page, Quote, Scrolled up/down, Top, Back, End: Answer, End: Nonsense/Controversial

metrics.name: Human preference
metrics.definition: Share of comparisons where WebGPT answer preferred, ties as 50%, for overall usefulness, coherence, factual accuracy

metrics.name: TruthfulQA truthful / truthful and informative
metrics.definition: Human evaluation for WebGPT; automated metric for GPT-3 baselines

metrics.name: Validation RM score
metrics.definition: Score of a 175B validation RM, Elo; 1 point = sigmoid(1) ~73% preference

eval.protocol: Human comparisons by contractors; error bars +/-1 standard error; detailed instructions for demonstration comparison, minimal instructions and new contractors for ELI5 reference comparison; no seeds reported

availability.data: Comparison dataset of 19,578 items released at openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net/webgpt-answer-viewer/comparisons.jsonl

limits: Out-of-distribution questions: WebGPT still quotes unreliable sources on TruthfulQA and can make more mistakes than humans there (Sec 6.1, 6.2)
Subtle hallucinations were hard for labelers to spot so non-imitative falsehoods were not tested directly
Reference-based evaluation incentivizes cherry-picking convincing references and accepting questions' implicit assumptions (Sec 6.4)
Question stance experiment is small (60 questions) and inconclusive (App H)
No compute, hardware or seeds reported; no code or weights released; RL used no EMA for 760M/13B RMs due to a bug
Rejection sampling vs RL comparison confounded by RL hyperparameter tuning and RM overoptimization; validation RM predictor expected to overestimate for large n

terms.definition: False statements that are incentivized by the training objective (even in the limit of infinite data and compute), such as reproducing common misconceptions
False statements that are the result of the model failing to achieve its training objective, including most hallucinations
